questions.q: Which three concrete next steps does this lesson give for scaling SQL Pete?
options: A larger base model, more schemas beyond Northwind/AdventureWorks2012, and real human preference data replacing the programmatic reward
Switching to a different programming language, adding a GUI, and renaming the assistant
Running the same experiment again with no changes
Removing RLHF and relying on SFT alone
questions.explain: The lesson names a larger base model, more schemas, and real human raters in place of the programmatic reward as the concrete next steps for scaling SQL Pete.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the Chapter 5 circuit finding is 'a data point, not a theory'?
options: Because the finding was proven false
Because it was tested on only one entity type (country names) and hasn't been checked on other entity types or at larger scale
Because interpretability research isn't real research
Because the circuit was never actually found
questions.explain: The lesson frames the single finding, on one entity type at one scale, as a starting point that needs testing on other entity types (like product names or dates) and at larger scale before it becomes a broader theory.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect the lab's RLHF pipeline to the AI Safety & Alignment course?
options: It claims the two are unrelated topics
It frames this lab's simplified, programmatic reward and interpretability tools as a working preview of the same reward-gaming and model-inspection issues at larger scale
It says the AI Safety & Alignment course replaces the need for this lab
It says SQL Pete will be directly reused without changes in that course
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly calls this lab's RLHF pipeline a deliberately simplified, real preview of the reward-gaming and interpretability issues the AI Safety & Alignment course covers at larger scale.

questions.q: What does this lesson identify as the transferable skill the whole lab was built to teach?
options: Memorizing the exact hyperparameters used in Project 3
The combination of scoping a question, building the system, and reporting the result honestly, demonstrated across all three projects
Writing Python code quickly
Passing a certification exam
questions.explain: The lesson states that the combination across all three projects — not any single one — is the transferable skill: scoping a question, building the system, and reporting results honestly.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what kind of safety-relevant behavior in SQL Pete is suggested as a target for further interpretability work?
options: Its ability to format SQL syntax with correct indentation
Its refusal to generate anything beyond a SELECT statement
Its response time when generating queries
Its choice of variable names in generated code
questions.explain: The lesson suggests looking for a circuit behind SQL Pete's refusal to generate anything beyond a SELECT statement, since that refusal is a safety-relevant behavior worth understanding on its own.
